pl-l4d14c3-d1e115.summary: Interprets Ambrose's 'some are found' and 'as one baptism, so one penance' as said not of the general but of the special custom of the Church concerning solemn penance, which among some is not repeated once celebrated.

pl-l4d14c3-d1e127.summary: Applies the same to Ambrose's 'penance once usurped and not truly celebrated takes away the fruit of the former and loses the use of the following': it concerns solemn penance.

pl-l4d14c3-d1e133.summary: Defines solemn penance, after Ambrose: penance done outside the church in public, in ashes and sackcloth, imposed only for graver, horrible, and manifest crimes; it is not to be repeated out of reverence for the sacrament, lest it become cheap and contemptible.
claims: Solemn penance is public, for grave notorious crimes.
It is not repeated, lest it be cheapened.

pl-l4d14c3-d1e140.summary: Quotes Augustine: though it is wisely provided that the place of that humblest penance be granted only once in the Church, lest the medicine become cheap, who would dare say to God: why do you spare again this man who after his first penance entangles himself again in sin?
claims: Solemn penance is granted once, but God's mercy is not limited.

pl-l4d14c3-d1e149.summary: Quotes Origen: faults not mortal, in speech or conduct, can always be repaired by penance; but for graver crimes the place of penance is granted only once; common sins, which we often incur, always receive penance and are always redeemed.
claims: Lesser faults can always be repaired.
For graver crimes the place of penance is given once.

pl-l4d14c3-d1e158.summary: Interprets 'common sins' as venial sins and perhaps some less grave mortal ones, frequently committed and frequently redeemed by penance; for graver crimes penance is done once, namely solemn penance, but if they are repeated penance is repeated, though not solemn; a practice not observed in some churches.
claims: Penance is repeated for repeated crimes, but not solemn penance.

pl-l4d14c3.summary: Explains Ambrose's 'one penance as one baptism' as referring not to the general but to the special custom of the Church concerning solemn penance, which in some places is not repeated once celebrated; likewise his saying about penance usurped and not truly celebrated. Solemn penance is done publicly outside the church in ashes and sackcloth for graver, notorious crimes, and is not repeated out of reverence for the sacrament. Augustine and Origen agree: the place of that humblest penance is granted once, but God's mercy is not limited; common sins, venial and some lesser mortal ones, are often redeemed by penance, while for graver crimes solemn penance is given once, though penance itself can be repeated, a practice not kept in some churches.
claims: Solemn penance is public, for grave notorious crimes, and is not repeated.
Penance in general can be repeated.
Common sins are frequently redeemed by penance.
